Add a large light-gray (#EFEFEF) rectangle with a thin red border from ~9% to ~91% width and ~25% to ~85% height as the content panel. 3. Insert a centered text box at top with 'POOLING' — Calibri bold, ~40pt, #C00000, all caps. 4. Inside the panel's upper-left, add a bullet list: main hollow-circle bullet 'Aggregate multiple values into a single value' (~20pt, #3B3B3B), then three indented smaller hollow-circle sub-bullets: 'Invariance to small transformations'; 'Reduces the size of the layer output/input to next layer → Faster computations'; 'Keeps most important information for the next layer'. 5. Below the list, draw two stacked rectangles (~200 px wide, thin #3333CC outline, no fill): first contains hollow-circle bullet 'Max pooling', second contains hollow-circle bullet 'Average pooling' (~18pt, #3B3B3B). 6. Build the bottom diagram left-to-right: (a) a 2x2 table with bright green (#3CB43C) cells and thin black borders, cells labeled bold lowercase a, b (top row) and c, d (bottom row); (b) a hollow block arrow (white fill, black outline) pointing right; (c) one green (#3CB43C) square with black border labeled bold 'z'; (d) italic text 'Pool' + '('; (e) a photo of a tiger leaping over water (~2:1 aspect); (f) ')'; (g) '=='; (h) the same tiger photo resized to ~40-45%; (i) beneath it a blue (#3333CC), bold, underlined caption 'Size is reduced'. 7. Do not add the bottom black strip — it is the video player's control bar, not slide content.
